title: Reddit Founder Says Building Social Media Apps Is ‘Not Cool Anymore’
gist: At the WIRED World Fair, Reddit cofounder Alexis Ohanian (now running Seven Seven Six, $1.3B+ AUM) argued social media app building is 'not cool anymore', expects a better group chat to become the next form of user-generated content, and backs the Dead Internet Theory as AI agents displace human users. The piece notes Reddit's AI data-licensing upside versus a 29% share drop after warning that Google's AI search was hurting referral traffic.

insights.claim: Alexis Ohanian says building social media apps is 'not cool anymore' and expects an improved version of the group chat to become the next major form of user-generated content.
insights.speaker: Isabella Ward
insights.so_what: A prominent VC signals capital rotating away from open social feeds toward private, group-chat-style platforms.
insights.quote: I'm expecting some better version of the group chat to be that new version of UGC

insights.claim: Ohanian's venture firm Seven Seven Six, with over $1.3 billion in assets under management, focuses on sports, which he sees as real-life community in an age of AI slop and a manipulated internet.
insights.speaker: Isabella Ward
insights.so_what: Offline, authentic-community assets like sports are being positioned as a hedge against AI-degraded online content.

insights.claim: Ohanian endorses the Dead Internet Theory and predicts human-oriented user interfaces will fade as more of the internet is built for AI agents to use rather than people.
insights.speaker: Isabella Ward
insights.so_what: An agent-first web threatens ad- and traffic-based business models built on human eyeballs.
insights.quote: more of the internet is going to get created for these agents to use, [rather] than for people.

insights.claim: Ohanian argues the internet has become heavily manipulated precisely because online conversation is so valuable, and calls for 'provable humanity on the internet without being creepy'.
insights.speaker: Isabella Ward
insights.so_what: Points to demand for human-verification and anti-bot infrastructure as an investable category.
insights.quote: there has to be provable humanity on the internet without being creepy

insights.claim: Reddit has licensed its archive of human conversations to Google and OpenAI for AI training, which Ohanian says made platforms like Reddit very valuable to LLMs.
insights.speaker: Isabella Ward
insights.so_what: Data licensing is a real revenue stream for human-content platforms in the AI era.
insights.quote: Platforms like ours became very, very valuable to LLMs

insights.claim: Reddit shares plunged 29 percent the week before the WIRED World Fair talk after the company warned that Google's AI-powered search was hurting referral traffic.
insights.speaker: Isabella Ward
insights.so_what: AI search cannibalizing referral traffic is a material, already-priced risk for content platforms dependent on Google.

insights.claim: Reddit said it would require users to sign in to fight third-party scraping and sustain engagement.
insights.speaker: Isabella Ward
insights.so_what: Login walls protect licensable data value but may trade off reach and traffic.

themes.theme: AI optimism from an Anthropic investor

insights.claim: Ohanian, an early Anthropic investor, is optimistic about AI, especially for medical breakthroughs, while acknowledging a real chance it causes significant harm.
insights.speaker: Isabella Ward
insights.so_what: Reflects investor sentiment that AI healthcare applications are a key upside case.
